objective: GET /events/records/holders also returns each record's top three entries, so a Historical card can show the top three without another read.
acceptance_criteria: Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation; the implementation commit edits no test.

Each non-null holder gains `top`: the record list's first three entries (fewer when the list holds fewer), each a RecordEntryOut exactly as GET /events/records/{id} returns it at the same positions (rank, value, figures, team, player, season, game), in list order. A test compares `top` with the list route's first page of limit 3 for a team record, a player single-game record and a player season record, including a tie at rank 1.
Every existing holder field (the first entry and tied_count) is unchanged; null holders stay null.
Still at most one statement per asked id, each fetching at most three rows; the Cache-Control header, the 24-id limit and the 422 rules are unchanged.
The PR records the route's time for 24 ids on the dev fixture before and after (median of 5).

The containerized backend suite, ruff and mypy pass. backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts are regenerated from the app and committed with the implementation; wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02-events.md is updated where this unit changes a documented fact.
